import pandas as pd
import seaborn as sns
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import io
import matplotlib.ticker as mticker

# Prepare the data
csv_data = """brand,model_year,megapixels,max_iso,weight_grams,price_usd,sensor_type,has_video_4k,lens_mount,body_type
Leica,2005,13.5,25600,324,811.8,Micro 4/3,1,E,Compact
Fuji,2019,46.4,51200,1151,3596.41,APS-C,0,EF,Mirrorless
Pentax,2012,38.7,12800,598,3357.2,Full Frame,0,MFT,Mirrorless
Olympus,2015,22.5,6400,1095,1555.7,APS-C,0,Z,Mirrorless
Leica,2016,12.2,25600,290,3899.09,Medium Format,0,MFT,DSLR
"""

df = pd.read_csv(io.StringIO(csv_data))

# Set a professional and visually appealing style
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid", context="talk")
fig, ax = plt.subplots(figsize=(14, 9))

# Create a rich scatter plot to explore multiple variables
# X-axis: Megapixels
# Y-axis: Price
# Hue (Color): Brand
# Size: Weight
# Style (Marker Shape): Body Type
scatter = sns.scatterplot(
    data=df,
    x='megapixels',
    y='price_usd',
    hue='brand',
    size='weight_grams',
    style='body_type',
    palette='viridis',
    sizes=(200, 2000),
    alpha=0.8,
    edgecolor='black',
    linewidth=1.5,
    ax=ax
)

# Add annotations to each point for clarity
for i, row in df.iterrows():
    ax.text(row['megapixels'] + 0.5,
            row['price_usd'],
            f"{row['brand']}\n({row['model_year']})",
            fontdict={'size': 10, 'color': 'dimgray', 'weight': 'semibold'},
            verticalalignment='center')

# --- Customize Plot for Clarity and Insight ---

# Set title and labels
ax.set_title('Camera Price vs. Megapixels', fontsize=24, weight='bold', pad=20)
ax.set_xlabel('Megapixels (MP)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)
ax.set_ylabel('Price (USD)', fontsize=16, labelpad=15)

# Format the y-axis to display as currency
formatter = mticker.FormatStrFormatter('$%.0f')
ax.yaxis.set_major_formatter(formatter)

# Adjust tick label size
ax.tick_params(axis='both', which='major', labelsize=12)

# Move the legend outside the plot to prevent overlap
ax.legend(title='Legend', bbox_to_anchor=(1.05, 1), loc='upper left', borderaxespad=0.)

# Adjust layout to make space for the legend
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 0.85, 1])

# Save the resulting visualization
plt.savefig('output.png', dpi=300, bbox_inches='tight')
